name: Southern Shrimp & Grits
steps: Pour the water, 1 cup of the shrimp stock, and 1 cup of the heavy cream into a saucepan. Whisk in the hominy grits and half of the salt, then cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, stirring often, until the hominy grits are thick and soft.
Cut the bacon into short pieces. Cook it in a wide skillet over medium heat for 6 minutes until the fat renders and the edges are crisp. Lift the bacon out and leave the drippings in the pan.
Mince the onion and the garlic. Cook them in the bacon drippings over medium heat for 3 minutes until the onion turns translucent.

Pat the shrimp dry, toss with the rest of the salt, and add them to the skillet. Cook over medium-high heat for 2 minutes until they are pink on the outside and still slightly translucent in the center. Transfer them to the plate with the bacon.
Pour the remaining shrimp stock into the skillet and scrape up the browned bits. Add the remaining heavy cream. Boil for 4 minutes until the liquid coats a spoon.
Stir in the black pepper, the cayenne pepper, the paprika, and the chile flakes. Return the bacon and the shrimp and cook on low for 2 minutes until the shrimp are opaque and reach 145°F (63°C).
Take the skillet off the heat. Stir in the lime juice and the butter. Slice the scallions. Spoon the shrimp over the hominy grits and scatter the scallions on top.

attribution.note: Reworded for 4 servings. Salt set to 1 tsp, black pepper to 1/2 tsp, and butter to 1 tbsp because the page left them unmeasured. Cayenne pepper, paprika, chile flakes, and lime juice were given amounts for the same reason. Water was added so the hominy grits can cook. Sherry is named in the method but not in the ingredient list, so the pan is reduced with shrimp stock instead. A flour-butter thickener was left out.

name: Chinese Egg Drop Soup
steps: Whisk the eggs in a bowl until the yolks and whites are fully blended.
Stir the cornstarch into the water until the slurry is smooth with no dry pockets.
Slice the scallions thin. Peel and mince the ginger.
Pour the chicken broth into a saucepan. Add the ginger and the salt. Warm it over medium heat for 5 minutes until it passes 165°F (74°C) and simmers with steam on the surface.
Stir the cornstarch slurry into the simmering chicken broth. Cook 1 minute until the soup looks lightly glossy.
Pour the eggs in a thin stream while you stir the soup in one direction. Cook 30 seconds until soft ribbons set and no raw egg remains.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the white pepper and the sesame oil. Ladle into bowls and top with the scallions.

attribution.note: No Chinese egg-drop page. Stracciatella is an Italian soup and was not cited as egg drop.

name: Filipino Garlic Fried Rice
steps: Break the cooked rice apart with damp fingers so the grains are separate and no large clumps remain.
Peel the garlic and mince it. Keep half of the minced garlic aside for the end.
Warm the vegetable oil in a wide skillet over medium heat for 1 minute until it shimmers.
Fry the first half of the garlic in the vegetable oil for 1 minute until it turns pale gold and smells sweet. Scoop it onto a plate before the pieces darken.
Raise the heat to medium-high. Add the cooked rice and the salt. Toss and press for 5 minutes until the grains are hot and a few edges crisp.
Return the fried garlic to the skillet and add the remaining raw garlic. Toss for 1 minute until the fresh garlic smells fragrant and the cooked rice is evenly salted.

attribution.note: No sinangag page. Com Chien is Vietnamese fried rice and was not cited as garlic fried rice.

name: Pan-Fried Pork Chops with Mashed Potatoes
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch chunks. Put them in a pot with the water and the salt.
Brush both sides of the pork rib chops with the cider vinegar, then press the chop rub into the meat.
Boil the potatoes over high heat for 18 minutes until a knife slides through a chunk easily. Drain the pot.
Warm the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the pork rib chops for 3 minutes on each side until a deep brown crust forms.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Transfer the skillet to the oven and roast until the center of a pork rib chop reaches 145°F (63°C), about 10 to 12 minutes.
Move the pork rib chops to a plate and rest them for 3 minutes so the juices settle.
Mash the drained potatoes with the butter and the milk until the mash is creamy and spreadable.
Season the potatoes with the black pepper. Serve the rested pork rib chops on the mash.

attribution.sourceTitle: Cookbook:Pan-Seared Pork Chops and Cookbook:Mashed Potatoes
attribution.note: Chops and mash from the two sources, kept at 4 servings. Pork cooked to 145°F (63°C) and rested 3 minutes. Salt set to 1 tbsp to match the potato pot in the method. Black pepper set to 1/2 tsp. Optional nutmeg was left out. Cider vinegar set to 2 tbsp because the page said as needed.

name: Cajun Red Beans & Rice
steps: Cover the red beans with plenty of water and soak them overnight. Drain before cooking. That soak is not included in the timed total.
Put the ham hocks, the celery, the onion, the bell pepper, the bay leaves, and the seafood seasoning in a large pot with 6 cups of fresh water. Cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Lower the heat and simmer for 60 minutes until the ham hocks are fork-tender and the meat starts to pull from the bone. Skim off the fat.
Lift out the ham hocks. Ladle off some of the liquid, add the drained red beans, and pour back enough cooking liquid to just cover the red beans.
Simmer the red beans for 45 minutes, stirring often, until they begin to break and the liquid looks creamy. Add a splash of the saved liquid if the pot looks dry.
Return the ham hocks and cook 45 minutes more until the red beans are soft and the ham meat is tender, well above 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the hot sauce and pull out the bay leaves. Spoon the red beans and ham beside the cooked rice.

attribution.note: Rice from the source is kept, already cooked. Scaled to about half for 4 servings: the page used 1 pound of red beans, 6 ham hocks, and 4 cups of cooked rice. Overnight soak excluded from the time. Hot sauce set to 2 tsp from the halved tablespoon.

name: Swedish Meatball Skillet
steps: Stir the milk and the bread crumbs together in a bowl and leave them for 8 minutes until the bread crumbs swell.
Grate the onion. Add it to the bowl with the ground beef, the ground pork, the egg, the salt, and the black pepper. Mix just until the meat looks even.
Roll the mixture into round meatballs about 1 inch across.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat until it foams.
Add the meatballs and fry for 8 minutes, turning so every side browns. They are done when the center reaches 160°F (71°C) and no pink remains.
Take the skillet off the heat and let the meatballs sit 2 minutes in the butter before serving from the pan.

attribution.note: Reworded. Meatballs cooked to 160°F (71°C). Milk chosen for the liquid. Salt set to 1 tsp, black pepper to 1/2 tsp, and butter to 1 tbsp. Mashed potatoes, brown sauce, and lingonberry are serving ideas on the page and are not ingredients, so they were left out. Yield kept at 4 servings.

name: Grilled Cheese & Tomato Soup
steps: Warm the olive oil in a soup pot over medium heat for 30 seconds until it shimmers.
Add the yellow onion, the salt, and the black pepper. Cook 3 minutes, stirring, until the yellow onion softens.
Add the white beans with their liquid, the garlic cloves cut in half, the dried oregano, and the sage. Simmer 4 minutes.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, the tomato paste, the crushed red pepper, and the water. Simmer 8 minutes until the tomatoes taste sweet and the soup thickens slightly.

Take the pot off the heat. Break in the cream cheese and blend until the soup is smooth. Return it to low heat for 10 minutes, stirring so the bottom does not scorch. It is ready when it is hot and velvety.
Tear the basil. Stir most of it into the soup and save a few pieces for the bowls.
Butter one side of each slice of bread. Heat a skillet over medium heat. Lay in four slices, buttered side down, and cook about 3 minutes until the undersides are golden.

Flip those slices, lay on the cheddar cheese, and cover with the remaining bread, buttered side up. Press with a spatula and cook about 3 minutes per side until the cheddar cheese melts and both outsides are browned. Cut and serve with the soup.

attribution.sourceTitle: Cookbook:Grilled Cheese Sandwich and Cookbook:Creamy Tomato and Bean Soup
attribution.note: Sandwich and soup from the two sources. Soup scaled toward 4 bowls: tomatoes, tomato paste, cream cheese, garlic, sage, basil, and water were reduced from the large pot, and the white beans stayed at one can. Four sandwiches were built from the single-sandwich method. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. The oven method for the sandwich was not used.

name: Sloppy Joes
steps: Chop the onion and the green bell pepper into small pieces.
Cook the ground beef with the onion and the green bell pepper in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes, breaking the meat apart, until the ground beef reaches 160°F (71°C) and no pink remains.
Drain the fat from the skillet and return the ground beef mixture to the pan.
Keep the heat at medium. Stir in the ketchup, the barbecue sauce, the garlic powder, and the chili powder until the meat is coated.
Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and clings to the ground beef.
Keep the skillet at a low bubble for 1 minute more until the ketchup and the barbecue sauce look glossy and the onion is fully soft.

attribution.note: Beef cooked to 160°F (71°C). Optional onion and green bell pepper were kept. Hamburger buns are named only in the serving line and are not an ingredient, so the recipe stops at the sauced beef and the name follows the source dish. Yield kept at 4 servings.

name: Erwtensoep (Split Pea Soup)
steps: Rinse the green split peas and soak them overnight in plenty of water. Drain them before cooking. The soak is not part of the timed total.
Slice the pork belly into strips. Brown the strips in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes until they are golden but still tender. Set them aside.
Simmer the drained green split peas in 6 cups of fresh water over medium heat for 30 minutes, skimming the foam, until the peas start to soften.

Chop the carrot, the leek, the onion, the celeriac, and the potatoes. Chop the pork belly bacon. Add all of them to the pea pot with the browned pork belly, the bay leaves, the salt, and the black pepper.
Simmer for 45 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the green split peas have broken into a thick soup. Add some of the remaining water if the pot looks dry.
Slice the smoked sausage and add it. Simmer 15 minutes more until the smoked sausage is heated through, at least 160°F (71°C), and the soup holds a spoon. Remove the bay leaves.

attribution.note: Mint is not in the source, so the name follows Erwtensoep. Amounts were set for 4 servings because the page left them open. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Fried dried onions appear only in the method, not the ingredient list, so they were left out. Overnight soak excluded from the time.

name: Argentine Chimichurri Steak
steps: Chop the flat-leaf parsley, the onion, and the garlic. Mix them with the dried oregano, the paprika, the red chile flakes, 3/4 tsp of the salt, and 1/4 tsp of the black pepper.

Boil the white wine vinegar and the water, then pour the hot liquid over the herb mixture. Stir and let it stand 30 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp of the olive oil. Cover and refrigerate overnight so the flavors soften. That rest is not counted in the cooking time. Set the sauce out 30 minutes before serving and stir it.
Mix the dried rosemary, the dried thyme, the smoked paprika, the chili powder, the garlic powder, the remaining salt, and the remaining black pepper.
Brush the strip steaks with the remaining olive oil and coat both sides with the spice mix. Leave the strip steaks at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Heat a grill with one zone hot and one zone medium. Sear the strip steaks on the hot side for about 1 minute, rotate them a quarter turn, and cook 1 minute more. Flip and repeat on the second side.
Move the strip steaks to the medium zone and cook, turning often, until the center reads 145°F (63°C) for medium.
Rest the strip steaks under foil for 8 minutes. Slice them across the grain and spoon the herb sauce over the slices.

attribution.note: Steak cooked, then dressed with the chimichurri. Scaled to 2 servings from 4 steaks, and the sauce scaled to about a quarter of the large batch. Optional add-ins were left out. Overnight rest excluded from the time. Olive oil on the steaks set to part of 3 tbsp because the page left that oil unmeasured. Doneness stated as medium.

name: Malaysian Peanut Noodles
steps: Boil a pot of water, add the salt, and cook the rice noodles until they are tender but still springy, about 5 minutes. Drain and rinse them under cold water.
Mince the garlic. Slice the scallions and the cucumber.
Warm the vegetable oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds until it smells sweet.
Stir in the peanut butter, the tamari, the lime juice, the brown sugar, the chile flakes, and the 1/3 cup of water. Simmer 2 minutes until the sauce is smooth and glossy.
Toss the rice noodles with the sauce over low heat for 1 minute until every strand is coated and hot.
Add the bean sprouts and toss for 30 seconds until they lose their raw edge. Top the bowls with the cucumber and the scallions.

attribution.note: No Malaysian peanut-noodle page. Gado-gado is a salad and was kept for r79.

name: Russian Beet Borscht
steps: Slice the potatoes and the beets thin. Put them in a saucepan with the water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 25 minutes until both are tender.
Melt the butter in a soup pot over medium heat. Add the onion and the salt. Cook 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is translucent.
Add the celery, the carrot, the cabbage, and 1 cup of the potato cooking water. Cover and cook 10 minutes until the cabbage is tender.
Add the potatoes, the beets, the rest of their cooking water, the black pepper, 1 tsp of the dill weed, the cider vinegar, the honey, and the tomato puree.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes until the soup tastes bright and the vegetables are fully soft. If it seems thin, simmer uncovered for 3 minutes more.
Ladle into bowls, add the sour cream, and sprinkle with the remaining dill weed.

attribution.note: Reworded and scaled slightly for 4 hearty bowls. Honey chosen instead of brown sugar. Black pepper set to 1/2 tsp because the page said a little. Butter kept at 1 tbsp.

name: Roast Chicken Dinner
steps: Heat the oven to 390°F (200°C). Pat the chicken dry.
Halve the lemon. Rub half of the salt inside the cavity of the chicken, then tuck both lemon halves inside.
Use part of the olive oil to film a roasting pan. Rub the rest of the olive oil over the chicken skin and season the outside with the remaining salt and the black pepper.
Roast the chicken for 20 minutes per pound plus 30 minutes. For this 4 lb chicken, plan on about 110 minutes, and start checking before the end.
The chicken is done when the thickest part of the thigh reaches 165°F (74°C) and the juices from that spot run clear.
Loosely cover the chicken and rest it for 20 minutes before carving.

attribution.note: Chicken to 165°F (74°C) in the thigh. Salt set to 1 tsp, black pepper to 1/2 tsp, and olive oil to 1 tbsp because the page left them unmeasured. Timing uses a 4 lb bird with the page's 20 minutes per pound plus 30 minutes, then a 20 minute rest. Servings kept at 6.

name: French Canadian Shepherd's Pie
steps: Peel the potatoes. Boil them in the water with half of the salt over high heat for 20 minutes until they are soft. Drain.
Mash the potatoes with the butter and the milk until the mash spreads easily with a spoon.
Chop the onion and the green bell pepper. Brown them with the ground beef in a skillet over medium heat for 10 minutes until the ground beef reaches 160°F (71°C). Drain the fat.
Spread the ground beef mixture in a casserole dish. Spoon the drained corn over the beef.
Spread the mashed potatoes over the corn to cover it. Season the top with the remaining salt and the black pepper.
Bake uncovered at 400°F (200°C) for 30 minutes until the potato surface is golden.

attribution.note: Beef base kept and named for the source. Ground beef cooked to 160°F (71°C). Salt set to 1 tbsp for the potato water and the top. Black pepper set to 1/2 tsp. Water added to boil the potatoes. Paprika and pickled beets are mentioned only as extras and are not ingredients, so they were left out. Yield kept near 6 servings.

name: Dal Makhani (Black Gram with Cream)
steps: Rinse the black gram and the kidney beans. Soak them overnight, then drain. The soak is not included in the time.
Simmer the black gram and the kidney beans in the water with 1 tsp of the salt, the red chile powder, the turmeric powder, and the grated ginger for 60 minutes until both are soft.
Warm the ghee in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the hing powder, the bay leaves, the cinnamon, the cloves, and the chopped onion. Cook 8 minutes until the onion is light brown.
Stir in the ginger garlic paste, then the chopped tomatoes and the coriander powder. Cook 6 minutes until the tomatoes break down into a paste.
Add the cooked black gram and kidney beans. Splash in a little water if the pot is stiff. Simmer 15 minutes until the dal is creamy and the whole spices smell warm.
Stir in the fresh cream and the clarified butter. Simmer 5 minutes. Add the remaining salt, scatter the coriander leaves on top, and lift out the bay leaves and the cinnamon before eating.

attribution.note: The page is dal makhani, not a rice plate, so rice was left out. Chickpeas are named in one method line but are not an ingredient. Ghee chosen for the cooking fat. Salt set where the page said to taste. Overnight soak excluded. Yield kept at 4 servings.

name: Portuguese Kale Sausage Soup
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into small cubes. Slice the onion, mince the garlic, and slice the smoked sausage into rounds. Strip the kale off the stems and slice it thin.
Warm the olive oil in a soup pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until it softens.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until it smells sweet.
Add the potatoes, the water, and the salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender enough to mash.
Mash a few of the potatoes against the side of the pot so the broth turns silky. Add the smoked sausage and simmer 5 minutes until the slices reach 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the kale and the black pepper. Cook 3 minutes until the kale is tender but still bright green.

attribution.note: No caldo verde page.

name: Indonesian Gado Gado
steps: Cover the eggs with water in a saucepan and boil for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm. Cool and slice them. Boil the potatoes in the same style of water for 20 minutes until tender, then peel them.
Warm 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the peeled potatoes for 5 minutes until the outsides are golden. Slice them.

In a small pan, fry the terasi, a fermented prawn paste, in a teaspoon of the vegetable oil for 1 minute until it smells toasty. Fry the peanuts in the remaining vegetable oil over medium heat for 4 minutes until they are golden. Cool them, then grind to a paste.
Grind the chile pepper, the garlic, the salt, the palm sugar, and the shallots into the peanut paste along with the fried terasi.
Scrape the paste into a saucepan with 1/2 cup of the water and the sugar. Bring it to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes until the sauce is thick. Stir in the lime juice and take the pan off the heat.
Shred the cabbage. Slice the cucumber and peel and slice the chayote. Boil the remaining water. Cook the cabbage for 4 minutes and the chayote for 6 minutes, until each is tender. Drain.
Using that hot water, cook the spinach and the water spinach for 1 minute, then the bean sprouts for 30 seconds. Drain each so they stay bright.

Arrange the cabbage, spinach, water spinach, bean sprouts, chayote, cucumber, potatoes, fried soybean cake, fried tempeh, and eggs on a platter. Pour the peanut sauce over them, scatter the fried shallots on top, and serve the kerupuk beside the salad.

attribution.note: Reworded for 4 servings. Peanuts and palm sugar scaled to about half. Salt set to 1 tsp and vegetable oil to 3 tbsp because the page left them open. Lime juice chosen instead of rice vinegar. Water added for the sauce and the vegetable pot. Asparagus beans were only an example and were left out. Terasi is fermented prawn paste, so the salad is not vegetarian.

name: German Mustard Schnitzel
steps: Pound the pork cutlets thin. Season both sides with the salt and the black pepper.
Set up three plates: the flour, the egg beaten until smooth, and the breadcrumbs. Dip each pork cutlet in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Warm the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Fry the pork cutlets for 3 minutes per side until the crust is golden and the center reaches 145°F (63°C).
Rest the pork cutlets on a plate for 3 minutes.
Pour off all but a thin film of vegetable oil. Add the mustard, the cream, and the water to the skillet. Simmer over medium heat for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats a spoon.
Return the pork cutlets to the pan just long enough to coat them in the mustard sauce, then serve.

attribution.note: No schnitzel page.

name: Colombian Bandeja Beans
steps: Rinse the red beans and soak them overnight in plenty of water. Drain. The soak is not included in the time.
Put the red beans in a pot with 6 cups of fresh water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 60 minutes until the red beans are almost tender.
Dice the pork belly, the onion, the tomatoes, and the scallions. Mince the garlic.
Warm the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the pork belly for 6 minutes until the fat renders and the pieces are browned and at least 160°F (71°C).
Add the onion and the scallions and cook 4 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, the tomatoes, and the ground cumin. Cook 5 minutes until the tomatoes collapse.
Stir that sofrito into the red beans with the salt. Simmer 15 minutes until the broth is thick and the red beans are fully soft. Add a splash of the remaining water if the pot looks dry.

attribution.note: No bandeja paisa page. Portuguese Feijoada is a different stew.

name: Egyptian Koshari
steps: Boil 2 cups of the water, stir in the rice and a pinch of the salt, cover, and cook on low for 15 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Boil the dried lentils in 3 cups of the water for 18 minutes until they are tender but still hold their shape. Drain.
Boil the small macaroni in the remaining salted water for 8 minutes until it is al dente. Drain.
Slice the onion thin and mince the garlic. Warm the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until it is deep gold and crisp at the edges. Lift it out.

In the same skillet, cook the garlic for 1 minute until it smells sweet. Add the chopped tomatoes, the tomato paste, the ground cumin, the ground cinnamon, the remaining salt, the black pepper, and the chile powder.
Simmer the tomato sauce on low for 12 minutes until it thickens and the spices taste rounded.
Layer the rice, the dried lentils, and the small macaroni in a dish. Spoon the tomato sauce over them, then top with the fried onion and the parsley.

attribution.sourceTitle: Cookbook:Koshari (Egyptian Rice with Pasta and Lentils)
attribution.note: Reworded. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Chile powder kept at 1/2 tsp. Parsley chosen for the garnish. Water added for the three pots. Yield kept at 4 servings.

sources.title: Cookbook:Koshari (Egyptian Rice with Pasta and Lentils)

name: Polish Pierogi Pan Fry
steps: Stir the salt, the egg, and the cold water together, then work them into the all-purpose flour until a shaggy dough forms.
Add the water a little at a time until the dough feels damp but not sticky. Knead in 2 tsp of the unsalted butter for 8 minutes until the dough is smooth.
Cover the dough and refrigerate it for 1 hour. A longer chill, up to a day, is optional and is not included in the time.
Roll the dough on a floured board to about 1/8 inch thick, using a little of the all-purpose flour to keep it from sticking. Cut circles.
Spoon the cheese filling into the center of each circle. Fold into half-moons and pinch the edges shut so no filling leaks.
Boil the pierogi in a pot of water, in two batches, for 6 minutes until they float and the dough is cooked through. Drain and rinse briefly so they do not stick.
Melt the remaining unsalted butter in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the pierogi for 4 minutes per side until both faces are golden.

attribution.note: Pan-fried after boiling. Dough scaled to about half for 4 servings. Cheese filling chosen. The 1 hour chill is included. A 24 hour rest is optional and excluded. Extra flour for rolling comes from the measured all-purpose flour.

name: Shrimp Curry
steps: Peel the shrimp if needed and pat them dry. Dice the onion and mince the garlic if it is not already minced.
Warm the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the shrimp and cook 2 minutes until they turn pink. Move them to a plate before they curl hard.
Melt the ghee in the same skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and the garlic and cook 4 minutes until the edges brown.
Stir in the curry powder and toast it for 30 seconds until it smells warm.
Add the chicken broth and the red curry paste. Simmer 3 minutes until the sauce looks glossy and slightly thick.
Return the shrimp and toss for 2 minutes on low until they are opaque and reach 145°F (63°C).

attribution.note: Name follows this shrimp curry, which uses curry powder and red curry paste rather than a Thai green curry paste. Shrimp cooked to 145°F (63°C). Yield kept at 4 servings.

name: Irish Colcannon
steps: Boil the potatoes, skins on if you like, for 20 minutes until they are soft. Drain them and shake the pot so the potatoes crumble.
Mash the potatoes. Stir in the salt, the black pepper, the mace, the paprika, and the single cream.
Cut 100 g of the unsalted butter into pieces and fold it into the mash. Cover the pot for 2 minutes so the unsalted butter melts, then stir again.
Shred the cabbage. Blanch it in boiling water for 2 minutes until it is bright and just tender. Drain.
Slice the leeks. Fry them in the remaining unsalted butter over medium heat for 4 minutes until soft, then add the cabbage and toss for 3 minutes.
Fold the cabbage and leeks into the mashed potatoes. Stir in most of the Gouda cheese.
Scatter the rest of the Gouda cheese on top. Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20 minutes until the Gouda cheese melts and the top browns.

attribution.note: Reworded for 4 servings, close to the page yield. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Mace and paprika were given amounts because the page left them open.

name: Senegalese Peanut Stew
steps: Cut the beef into cubes. Warm the vegetable oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef on all sides, about 6 minutes, then move it to a plate.
Chop the onion and mince the garlic. Cook them in the same pot over medium heat for 4 minutes until the onion is translucent.
Lower the heat. Stir in the peanut butter until it melts and coats the onion and the garlic.
Add the ground cumin, the paprika, the chile powder, the salt, and the black pepper. Stir in the diced tomatoes with their juice.
Pour in the beef broth a little at a time, stirring so the sauce stays smooth. Return the beef and coat it in the sauce. Cover and simmer on low for 30 minutes until the beef is becoming tender.

Dice the carrots, the potatoes, and the bell pepper. Slice the okra. Add them with the spinach. Cover and simmer 18 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the beef is fork-tender, at least 160°F (71°C).
Rest the pot off the heat for 5 minutes so the stew thickens. Scatter the cilantro on top.

attribution.note: Peanuts kept as peanut butter. Beef chosen, with beef broth, and spinach chosen for the greens. Scaled to about three quarters for 4 servings. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp.

name: Australian Lamb Chops
steps: Halve the garlic head. Rub the cut face over both sides of the lamb loin chops.
Chop the rosemary and the thyme. Mix them with the salt, the black pepper, the smoked paprika, and the cayenne pepper.
Brush the lamb loin chops with the olive oil and press the spice mix into the meat. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Heat a grill until the grate is very hot. Sear the lamb loin chops for 90 seconds, rotate them a quarter turn, and cook 90 seconds more. Flip and repeat.
Move the lamb loin chops to a medium zone and cook, turning often, until the center reaches 145°F (63°C) for medium.
Rest the lamb loin chops for 7 minutes before serving.

attribution.note: Lamb cooked and rested. Four chops kept for 2 servings, matching the page. Salt set to 1 tsp, black pepper to 1/2 tsp, and olive oil to 1 tbsp. Cayenne pepper reduced from the printed 4 tsp to 1 tsp so the chops stay edible. The 1 hour chill is included. Doneness stated as medium.

name: Chilean Corn Casserole
steps: Cover the eggs with water and boil for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm. Cool, peel, and quarter them.
Chop the onion. Warm the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the ground beef, the ground cumin, the paprika, the salt, and the black pepper. Cook 8 minutes, breaking the meat apart, until the ground beef reaches 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the raisins and the olives. Spread the mixture in a baking dish and nestle in the quartered eggs.
Blend the corn with the milk and the basil until the puree is mostly smooth with a little texture left.
Spread the corn puree over the beef. Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30 minutes until the top is set and golden at the edges.

attribution.note: No pastel de choclo page.

name: Georgian Cheese Flatbread
steps: Stir the sugar into the warm water. Sprinkle on the active dry yeast and wait 5 minutes until it foams.
Beat in 2 of the eggs and the flour. Knead on a floured board for 5 minutes until the dough is smooth, using a little of the flour if it sticks.
Set the dough in a greased bowl, cover it, and let it rise in a warm spot for 30 minutes until it doubles. Punch it down and let it rise 20 minutes more.
While the dough rises, crumble the feta cheese and grate the smoked provolone cheese and the Parmesan cheese. Mix them with the remaining 2 eggs.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Divide the dough in half. Roll one piece to fit a small baking sheet and lay it on the greased sheet.
Spread the cheese filling to within 1/2 inch of the edge. Roll the second piece of dough to the same size, lay it on top, and press the edges with a few drops of warm water to seal.
Bake for 10 minutes, then continue baking about 12 minutes more until the top is golden brown. Cool 5 minutes, then cut.

attribution.note: Cheese filling from the source kept. Scaled to about half for 4 servings. Salt is named in the method but not in the ingredient list, so it was left out. Butter for the top is also absent from the ingredient list and was left out. Both rises are included in the time.

name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (218°C).
Trim the bases of the Brussels sprouts, pull off loose leaves, and wash and dry them.
Halve the Brussels sprouts. Quarter any that are very large.
Toss the Brussels sprouts with the olive oil until each piece has a thin coat and none are dripping.
Season with the salt and the black pepper. Spread them on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once halfway, until the cut faces are brown and a sprout center is tender when pierced.

attribution.note: Honey and sesame are not in the source, so the name follows the roasted sprouts. Salt set to 1 tsp, black pepper to 1/2 tsp, and olive oil to 1 tbsp. Sprouts set at 1.5 lb for 4 servings.

name: Paella de Marisco
steps: Put the crab, the shrimp heads, the bay leaf, 4 cloves of the garlic, and the yellow onion into the water. Boil until the liquid reduces to about 1 liter, mashing the solids now and then so they give up their flavor, about 25 minutes. Strain and save the broth.
Warm the olive oil in a wide paella pan over medium heat. Add the mussels, cover just the center of the pan, and cook until they open, about 4 minutes. Lift them out and discard any that stay shut.
Salt the Norway lobsters lightly with a pinch of the salt. Sear them in the oil for 2 minutes per side, then remove them.
Dice the squid and add it. Cook 2 minutes. Add the shrimp and cook 2 minutes more until they turn pink and reach 145°F (63°C). Lift the seafood out.
Mince the remaining garlic and cook it in the pan for 1 minute until golden. Add the grated tomatoes and cook 4 minutes until the mixture looks like a thick sofrito.
Stir in the Valencian rice until every grain is coated. Add the sweet paprika and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the strained broth and the saffron threads. Add the rest of the salt.

Simmer, without constant stirring, until the Valencian rice is slightly firm at the center and the pan is moist rather than soupy, about 25 to 35 minutes. Nestle the Norway lobsters and the mussels back in for the last 5 minutes so they heat through.
Cover the pan with a towel and rest it off the heat for 5 minutes before serving.

attribution.note: Reworded and scaled toward 4 servings from the large pan. Unmeasured seafood, tomatoes, rice, onion, and salt were given amounts. Sweet paprika is what the page uses, so the name follows Paella de Marisco. Shrimp cooked to 145°F (63°C). Mussels are done when they open.

name: Rice Pudding
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
Whisk the milk, the eggs, and the sugar in a baking dish until the mixture looks frothy.
Stir in the cinnamon, the nutmeg, the vanilla extract, and the cardamom.
Fold in the cooked rice. Scatter the raisins on top without stirring, so they do not all sink.
Set the dish in a larger pan and pour in the water until it comes about 1 inch up the side.
Bake for 80 minutes until the center is just set and a knife comes out clean.

attribution.note: Coconut and lime are not in the source, so the name is rice pudding. Scaled to about one third of the large batch for 4 servings, using the page's cup measures rather than the conflicting liter figure. Water added for the baking bath. Cardamom kept.

name: Dark Chocolate Avocado Mousse
steps: Halve the avocados, lift out the pits, and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Mash the avocados with a fork until the flesh is mostly smooth and only a few small lumps remain.
Add the cocoa powder and mash until the color is even and no dry cocoa powder shows.
Add the agave syrup and stir for 1 minute until the mousse tastes balanced and looks glossy.
Taste and mash once more so the cocoa powder is fully blended.
Spoon the mousse into four cups and chill 5 minutes if you want a firmer set, then serve.

attribution.note: The page is an avocado and cocoa mousse, so it was used. Amounts were set for 4 servings because the page left them open.

name: Berry Chia Parfait
steps: Stir the chia seeds, the milk, the vanilla extract, and the honey in a bowl until no dry chia seeds remain.
Wait 5 minutes, then stir again so the chia seeds do not clump.
Cover and chill 10 minutes until the mixture thickens and a spoon stands up in it.
Spoon half of the chia mixture into two glasses.
Add a layer of berries and a spoon of the yogurt.
Repeat with the remaining chia mixture, berries, and yogurt.

attribution.note: No chia pudding or berry parfait page.

name: Banana Nutmeg Pancakes
steps: Warm a nonstick skillet over low heat while you mix the batter.
Whisk the all-purpose flour, the sugar, the salt, the baking powder, the baking soda, and the nutmeg in a bowl.
Warm the buttermilk and the milk for 20 seconds until they lose their chill. Whisk in the egg, the melted unsalted butter, and the vanilla extract.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry mixture and whisk until just combined. Stir in the water so the batter is thick but pourable.
Slice the bananas thin. Raise the skillet to medium and brush it with some of the vegetable oil. When the oil shimmers, pour in about 1/4 cup of batter for each pancake.

Lay 5 or 6 banana slices on each uncooked top. Cook 2 to 3 minutes until the bottoms are golden and bubbles set on the surface, then flip and cook until the second side is golden. Brush the skillet with the remaining vegetable oil between batches.

attribution.note: Distinct from plain banana pancakes. Vegetable oil set to 1 tbsp because the page left the griddle oil unmeasured. Water set to 1 tbsp to loosen the batter, as the method allows a spoonful. Yield kept at 4 servings.

name: Lemon Ricotta Toast
steps: Toast the bread in a skillet over medium heat with a little of the olive oil, about 2 minutes per side, until both faces are golden.
Zest the lemon and squeeze its juice.
Stir the ricotta with the lemon zest, half of the lemon juice, the honey, the salt, and the black pepper.
Spread the ricotta on the warm bread.
Drizzle the remaining olive oil and the rest of the lemon juice over the toasts.
Serve while the bread is still crisp and the ricotta is cool.

attribution.note: No lemon ricotta toast page.

name: Spiced Apple Crisp
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Stir the all-purpose flour, the brown sugar, the rolled oats, and the cinnamon together in a bowl.
Core and slice the baking apples. Spread them in an 8-inch baking dish.
Cut the cold butter into the flour mixture with two knives until it forms small crumbs and the butter does not smear.
Scatter the crumb topping over the baking apples and pat it lightly.
Bake for 30 minutes until the topping is deep brown and the baking apples bubble at the edges. A few dark spots are fine; pull it before the topping blackens.

attribution.note: Reworded and scaled to about two thirds for 4 servings. Cinnamon kept as the spice.

name: Date Bars
steps: Chop the dates. Combine them with the white sugar and the water in a saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring, for 10 minutes until the dates thicken into a paste. Cool the pan.
Beat the butter, the shortening, and the brown sugar together until creamy.
Stir the flour, the salt, the baking soda, and the quick-cooking oatmeal into that mixture to make a crumbly dough.
Grease a small baking pan. Press half of the crumb mixture into an even layer.
Spread the cooled date filling over the crumbs. Crumble the rest of the dough on top and press it lightly.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25 minutes until the top is light brown. Cut into bars while still warm.

attribution.note: No-bake bites replaced with the sourced date bars. Scaled to about one third for 4 servings.

name: Homestyle Chicken Noodle Soup
steps: Cover the dried mushrooms with hot water and let them soften for 15 minutes. Dice the yellow onion, mince the garlic, slice the carrots, and chop the celery and the parsley.
Put the all-purpose flour in a shallow bowl. Coat the chicken thighs lightly on all sides.

Warm the butter and the olive oil in a soup pot over medium-high heat. When the fat sizzles, add the chicken thighs and cook 6 minutes, turning, until they are lightly browned. The chicken is not finished yet. Move it to a board and cut it into bite-size pieces.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the yellow onion, the garlic, the thyme, the basil, and the rosemary. Cook 5 minutes until the yellow onion starts to brown.
Add the chicken broth and the water. Raise the heat and bring the pot to a simmer, about 200°F (93°C).

Drain the dried mushrooms and squeeze them dry. Add the chicken, the dried mushrooms, the peas, and the carrots. Simmer 5 minutes until the carrots are tender and the chicken thighs reach 165°F (74°C).
Add the pasta and the celery. Cook 6 minutes until the pasta is just tender.
Stir in the parsley and the juice of the lemon. Season with the salt and the black pepper.

attribution.note: Reworded. Chicken cooked to 165°F (74°C). Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Rosemary set to 1 tbsp because the page said a half-chopped amount. Yield kept at 8 servings.

name: Tahini Banana Nice Cream
steps: Peel the bananas, slice them, and freeze them until they are solid. Use bananas that are already frozen if you have them. The freeze itself can be done ahead and is not a long cook.
Break the frozen banana slices into a blender.
Add the tahini, the maple syrup, the vanilla extract, and the salt.
Blend, stopping to scrape the sides. Add the water a spoonful at a time until the mixture turns smooth and looks like soft ice cream.
Blend 20 seconds more until no banana chunks remain and the tahini is fully mixed.
Spoon into bowls and eat right away, while it is still thick.

attribution.note: No tahini banana ice or nice-cream page.

name: Mediterranean Chicken and Rice
steps: Cut the chicken into serving pieces if it is whole. Season it with the salt and the black pepper. Chop the onion, dice the red bell pepper, and mince the garlic.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken on all sides, about 8 minutes. Lift it out.

Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until it smells sweet and is not yet dark. Add the onion, the red bell pepper, the diced tomatoes, and the sweet paprika. Cook 6 minutes until the vegetables soften.
Add the cilantro, the chicken stock, and the saffron threads. Bring the pot to a rolling boil.
Stir in the long-grain rice. Cover and simmer over medium heat for 20 minutes until the long-grain rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Add a splash of water if the pot dries early.
Nestle the chicken into the rice, cover, and cook 8 minutes more until the thickest piece reaches 165°F (74°C).
Scatter the drained peas on top, cover for 2 minutes so they heat through, then serve.

attribution.note: Reworded. Chicken cooked to 165°F (74°C). Salt set to 1 tsp, black pepper to 1/2 tsp, and olive oil to 1 tbsp. Stock set to 6 cups, the page's parenthetical amount, rather than the conflicting 4 liter figure. A 3 lb chicken kept the pot at 4 servings.

name: Lamb Kofta
steps: Heat a broiler to moderate-high.
Grate the onion. Chop the parsley, the cilantro, and the spearmint.

Combine the ground lamb, the onion, the sweet paprika, the ground cumin, the ground cinnamon, the cayenne, the salt, the black pepper, the parsley, the cilantro, and the spearmint. Mix with your hands just until even.
Shape portions of about 2 tablespoons into oblong kofta about 3 inches long.
Set the kofta on a rack over a baking sheet. Broil about 5 minutes per side.
They are done when the outside is browned and the center reaches 160°F (71°C) with no pink remaining. Rest 3 minutes before serving.

attribution.note: Yogurt is not in the source, so the name is lamb kofta. Optional lamb fat was left out. Ground lamb cooked to 160°F (71°C). Yield kept at 4 servings.

name: Hummus (Greek)
steps: Drain the chickpeas. If they have skins, rub them under cold water so most of the skins slip off, then drain again.
Peel the garlic and chop it roughly so the pieces blend smooth.
Blend the lemon juice with the tahini until the mixture looks pale and smooth.
Add the chickpeas, the garlic, and the olive oil. Blend until the puree starts to climb the sides of the bowl.
Add the water a spoonful at a time and blend until the hummus is creamy and spreadable.
Stir in the salt and the black pepper. Taste and blend once more so the seasoning is even.

attribution.note: This hummus has no peppers and no flatbread, so it is served as hummus rather than wraps. Canned chickpeas were chosen, which skips the overnight soak and the long simmer. Scaled to about 2 cups of chickpeas for 4 servings from the very large batch. Water added to loosen the puree. Salt and black pepper kept in proportion.

name: Chipotle Sweet Potato Tacos
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (218°C). Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into 1/2-inch cubes.
Toss the sweet potatoes with the vegetable oil, the chipotle chile powder, the ground cumin, and the salt.
Spread them on a baking sheet. Roast for 22 minutes, turning once, until the edges brown and a cube is soft inside.
Dice the onion and chop the cilantro. Cut the lime into wedges.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 seconds per side until they flex.
Fill the corn tortillas with the sweet potatoes, the onion, and the cilantro. Squeeze the lime over the tacos.

attribution.note: No chipotle sweet-potato taco page. Vegetarian Soft Tacos is used for r32.

name: Creamy Tomato Tortellini
steps: Boil the cheese tortellini in salted water until they are just tender, about 4 minutes for fresh or as the package needs for dried. Drain.
Mince the garlic. Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds until it smells sweet.
Add the crushed tomatoes, the dried oregano, the salt, and the black pepper. Simmer 8 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in the cream and simmer 2 minutes until the sauce looks pale red and coats a spoon.
Add the cheese tortellini and toss for 1 minute until they are hot.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the Parmesan cheese and the torn basil.

attribution.note: No creamy tomato tortellini page. Tortellini in Sweet Potato Sauce is a different dish.

name: Pesto II
steps: Put a generous splash of the olive oil in a blender and start it running so the blades stay wet.
Drop in the fresh basil for pesto a handful at a time, adding more olive oil whenever the puree stalls.
Add the walnuts and blend until they disappear into the green puree.
Add the garlic and the rest of the olive oil. Blend until the sauce is fluid and the garlic is fully ground.
Add the Parmesan cheese and pulse just until it is mixed. The flavor should still be mostly fresh basil for pesto.
Scrape the pesto into a bowl. It should look glossy and thick enough to cling to a spoon.

attribution.note: Walnuts chosen instead of pine nuts. Gnocchi is not in this pesto, so the name follows the source. Amounts were set for about 1 cup, enough for 4 servings, because the page left them open. Garlic scaled from 7 cloves to 4 for that smaller batch.

name: Sheet-Pan Sausage & Fennel
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (218°C).
Trim the fennel bulbs, slice them into wedges, and cut the onion into wedges. Crush the fennel seed.
Toss the fennel bulbs and the onion with the olive oil, the salt, the black pepper, and the fennel seed. Spread them on a sheet pan.
Nestle the pork sausage among the vegetables.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning the pork sausage once, until the fennel bulbs are tender and browned and the pork sausage reaches 160°F (71°C).
Cut the lemon into wedges and squeeze them over the pan before serving.

attribution.note: No sausage-and-fennel page.

name: Falafel
steps: Soak the dried chickpeas for falafel overnight in plenty of water, then drain, rinse, and pat them dry. The soak is not included in the time.
Pulse the dried chickpeas for falafel in a food processor until they are a coarse puree, not a smooth paste.
Add the garlic, the parsley, the chopped onion, the ground coriander, the ground cumin, the cayenne pepper, the baking powder, and the flour. Process until the mixture holds together when squeezed.
Shape tablespoon-sized balls and flatten them slightly.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Fry the balls in batches for about 3 minutes per side until they are deep brown and crisp outside and hot in the center.
Drain on a rack and eat while the crust is still crisp.

attribution.note: Fried as the source writes, not baked. Pita is mentioned only in the last method line and is not an ingredient, so it was left out and the name follows the source. Overnight soak excluded. Yield kept for 4 servings from 2 cups of chickpeas.

name: Cider-Glazed Pork Chops
steps: Rub the grill seasoning over the pork rib chops. Refrigerate them for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, combine the apple cider, the cider vinegar, and the Worcestershire sauce in a saucepan. Boil over medium heat until the liquid reduces by about one third, about 8 minutes. Take it off the heat.
Heat a grill to high. Cook the pork rib chops, covered, for 2 minutes.
Brush with the cider mixture, rotate the pork rib chops a quarter turn, and cook 2 minutes more.
Flip and repeat the brush-and-turn pattern until the center of a pork rib chop reaches 145°F (63°C).
Rest the pork rib chops for 3 minutes. Serve with the remaining cider mixture.

attribution.note: Reworded. Pork cooked to 145°F (63°C) and rested 3 minutes. Grill seasoning set to 1 tbsp because the page said as needed. The 30 minute chill is included. Yield kept at 4 chops.

name: Mushroom Risotto
steps: Chop the white onion and mince the garlic. Slice the porcini mushrooms and chop the flat-leaf parsley. Keep the chicken stock hotter than 165°F (74°C), at a bare simmer, in a separate saucepan.
Melt half of the salted butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the white onion and the garlic for 4 minutes until the white onion is translucent and neither has browned.
Add the arborio rice and stir for 30 seconds until every grain is coated in the salted butter.
Pour in the dry white wine. Let it bubble until the pan is almost dry, about 2 minutes.
Add the chicken stock a ladle at a time, stirring every couple of minutes, and wait until each addition is absorbed before adding more.

After about 5 minutes, stir in the porcini mushrooms. Keep adding chicken stock until the arborio rice is tender with a little bite left and the risotto slowly spreads on a plate, about 18 minutes total.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the flat-leaf parsley, the remaining salted butter, and 2 tbsp of the Parmesan cheese. Serve the rest of the Parmesan cheese at the table.

attribution.note: Stock and mushrooms from the source kept. Fresh porcini chosen, so no soak. Yield kept near 4 servings from 250 g of arborio rice. Chicken stock means this is not a vegetarian risotto.

name: Spaghetti with Clams
steps: Bring the water and the salt to a boil in a large pot.
Add the spaghetti and cook for 8 minutes until it is al dente. Scoop out a little pasta water, then drain.
Scrub the live clams. Dice the plum tomatoes, mince the garlic, and chop the parsley.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic for 1 minute until it is golden but not dark.

Add the live clams and the plum tomatoes. Cover and cook for 8 minutes, shaking the pan every minute, until the clams open and the sauce is bubbling above 145°F (63°C). Discard any clam that stays shut.
Add the spaghetti, the black pepper, and a splash of pasta water if the pan looks dry. Toss over low heat until the spaghetti is coated. Scatter the parsley on top.

attribution.note: Clams from the source kept. Linguine was renamed because the page uses spaghetti. Salt set to 1 tbsp for the pasta water, matching the method. Olive oil set to 1 tbsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Optional canned clams and clam broth were left out. Black pepper chosen instead of peperoncino. Yield kept at 4 servings.

name: BBQ Chicken Flatbreads
steps: Stir 8 tbsp of the dark brown sugar, the salt, 4 cups of the water, the minced garlic, the lemon zest, and the chicken broth in a large bag or pot. Submerge the chicken thighs, the chicken legs, and the chicken breasts. Refrigerate for 2 hours. That brine is included in the time.
While the chicken brines, boil the tomato paste, the honey, the apple cider vinegar, and the Worcestershire sauce over medium-high heat until the sauce reduces by half, about 15 minutes.
Mix the paprika, the smoked paprika, the dried rosemary, the dried thyme, the cayenne pepper, the black pepper, and the remaining dark brown sugar.
Put the all-purpose flour in a bowl and make a well. Add the vegetable oil and the remaining water. Mix into a dough, then rest it for 1 hour. This rest fits inside the brine.
Lift the chicken out of the brine and pat it dry. Massage the spice rub over the chicken thighs, the chicken legs, and the chicken breasts. Refrigerate 30 minutes.

Divide the dough into 4 pieces. Stretch each piece very thin. Cook on a hot dry pan until bubbles appear, then flip and cook 40 seconds more, until the flatbreads are flexible with brown spots. Use a drop of vegetable oil on the grill grate as well.

Grill the chicken over a hot charcoal or gas fire, turning often, for 10 minutes. Keep turning and brush with the sauce until the chicken breasts reach 165°F (74°C) and the chicken thighs and chicken legs do too.
Rest the chicken under foil for 7 minutes. Boil any leftover sauce for 5 minutes. Slice the chicken and serve it on the flatbreads with the sauce.

attribution.note: Chicken is cooked, then served on the flatbread. No cheese was added. Brine salt, sugar, garlic, lemon zest, water, and chicken broth follow the page and the brine is discarded. Flatbread flour, water, and vegetable oil were given amounts because the page only said handfuls. The 2 hour brine is included. Dark-meat guidance on the page was aligned to 165°F (74°C) for all of the chicken. Yield kept at 4 servings.

name: Zucchini Fritters
steps: Grate the zucchini. Toss it with the salt and let it sit 10 minutes. Squeeze out the liquid.
Slice the scallions. Beat the eggs.
Stir the zucchini, the scallions, the eggs, the flour, and the black pepper into a thick batter.
Warm the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat until it shimmers.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the skillet and flatten them. Fry 3 minutes per side until both faces are deep golden and the center is set.
Drain on a rack and serve while the crust is still crisp.

attribution.note: No zucchini fritter page. Zucchini Pie and Zucchini Bread are different dishes.

name: Stuffed Bell Peppers
steps: Cook the parboiled rice in boiling water until it is tender, about 12 minutes. Drain.
Heat the oven to 390°F (200°C). Oil a baking dish with the vegetable oil and set the dish in the oven while it heats.
Cut the tops off the red bell peppers and pull out the seeds so each pepper stands like a cup.
Mix the parboiled rice, the egg, the ground beef, the salt, the black pepper, and the paprika.
Fill the red bell peppers and stand them in the oiled dish.
Bake for 45 minutes until the filling reaches 160°F (71°C) and the red bell peppers are tender.

attribution.note: Peppers from the source kept. Beef chosen for the ground meat. Rice set to 50 g from the page's parenthetical weight, and the filling scaled from 6 peppers to 4. Salt set to 1 tsp, black pepper to 1/2 tsp, paprika to 1 tsp, and vegetable oil to 1 tbsp. Ground beef cooked to 160°F (71°C). A side salad and extra tomato sauce are not ingredients and were left out.

name: Tuna Nicoise Salad
steps: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm. Cool them and cut into quarters. Trim the green beans and boil them for 4 minutes until just tender. Drain.

Season the tuna steak with a pinch of the salt. Sear it in a spoon of the olive oil over medium-high heat for about 3 minutes per side until the center reaches 145°F (63°C). Cut it into bite-size pieces.
Quarter the tomatoes and salt them lightly with some of the salt. Slice the cucumber, the green bell peppers, and the white onions. Cut the artichokes into rounds. Chop the basil. Halve the garlic.

Rub a large bowl with the cut garlic. Add the green beans, the artichokes, the green bell peppers, the white onions, the cucumber, the eggs, the tuna steak, the black olives, the capers, and the basil.
Drain the tomatoes, season them with the remaining salt, and add them to the bowl.
Stir the remaining olive oil with the black pepper and pour it over the salad. Chill until you are ready to eat.

attribution.note: Tuna chosen instead of anchovies. Egg, green beans, and the other salad foods the page lists were kept. Potatoes are not in this page. Olive oil set to 6 tbsp to match the method's six spoonfuls. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Tuna cooked to 145°F (63°C). Scaled slightly toward 4 servings.

name: Chicken Tikka
steps: Dice the chicken breast into cubes. Mince the garlic and chop the red chiles and the cilantro.

Stir the mustard seed oil, the milk, the plain yogurt, the lemon juice, the tomato paste, the cilantro, the garlic, the red chiles, the paprika, the garam masala, the cumin powder, the turmeric, and the salt in a non-metal bowl.

Add the chicken breast and turn it until every cube is coated. For the best flavor, cover and refrigerate up to 24 hours. That marinade is optional and is not included in the time. If you skip it, cook right away.
Thread the chicken breast on skewers. Heat a grill or broiler to medium.
Cook for 6 to 8 minutes per side, turning once.
The chicken breast is done when the cubes reach 165°F (74°C) and the meat breaks apart when pressed with a fork.

attribution.note: Lettuce is not in the ingredient list, so the chicken is served as tikka rather than in wraps. The long marinade is optional and is not included in the time. Chicken cooked to 165°F (74°C). Yield kept at 4 servings from 1.5 lb of chicken breast.

name: Pumpkin Soup
steps: Chop the onion. Dice the carrots, the potatoes, the zucchinis, and the pumpkin. Drain the chickpeas.
Warm the vegetable oil in a soup pot over medium heat until it shimmers.
Add the onion, the carrots, the potatoes, and the zucchinis. Cook 6 minutes until the onion softens.
Add the pumpkin and the chickpeas. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the water. Bring the pot to a simmer over medium heat.
Cook for 20 minutes until the carrots are soft and the pumpkin has started to fall apart. Mash a few pieces if you want a thicker soup.

attribution.note: Coconut is not in the source, so the name is pumpkin soup. Amounts were set for 4 servings because the page left them open. Vegetable oil set to 1 tbsp.

name: Broccoli Cheddar Frittata
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Chop the broccoli and the onion.
Warm the olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 3 minutes until it softens.
Add the broccoli and cook 4 minutes until it is bright green and just tender.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, the salt, and the black pepper.
Pour the eggs over the broccoli. Scatter the cheddar cheese on top. Cook on the stove for 3 minutes until the edges set.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake 12 minutes until the center is just set and no longer wet.

attribution.note: No broccoli cheddar frittata page. Asparagus Frittata was not relabelled as broccoli.

name: Sesame Soba Salad
steps: Boil the soba noodles until they are tender but still springy, about 4 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the soy sauce, the sesame oil, the rice vinegar, and the sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Slice the cucumber and the scallions. Grate the ginger.
Toss the soba noodles with the dressing and the ginger.
Fold in the cucumber and the scallions.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1 minute until they smell nutty, then scatter them over the salad.

attribution.note: No soba page. Sesame Noodle Salad is used for the sesame noodle recipes.

name: Steak and Mushrooms
steps: Brush the strip steaks with the olive oil. Season both sides with the salt and the black pepper.

Heat a grill until the grate is hotter than 145°F (63°C). Cook the strip steaks for 4 minutes per side, rotating them halfway through the first side, until the center reads 135°F (57°C) for medium-rare.
Rest the strip steaks for 5 minutes.
While they rest, slice the button mushrooms and dice the onion. Mince the garlic.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds until it turns gold.
Add the onion and the button mushrooms. Cook, tossing, for 5 minutes until the button mushrooms are browned and the onion is soft. Serve them with the strip steaks.

attribution.note: Garlic and butter are in the source and are used on the mushrooms. The steaks are grilled whole, so the name follows the source dish. Scaled to 2 steaks for 2 servings. Salt set to 1 tsp, black pepper to 1/2 tsp, and olive oil to 1 tbsp. Doneness stated as medium-rare.

name: Coconut Curry Mussels
steps: Scrub the mussels and pull off any beards. Discard any mussel that is cracked or that stays open after a tap.
Dice the onion and mince the garlic. Chop the cilantro and cut the lime into wedges.
Warm the vegetable oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until it softens.
Add the garlic and the curry powder. Stir for 30 seconds until the curry powder smells toasty.
Pour in the coconut milk, the salt, and the black pepper. Bring the broth to a simmer hotter than 145°F (63°C).
Add the mussels, cover, and cook 5 minutes until they open. Discard any that stay shut. Squeeze the lime over the pot and scatter the cilantro on top.

attribution.note: No coconut-curry mussel page. Moules marinière is a different dish.

name: Spinach Artichoke Quesadillas
steps: Blend the cream cheese, the heavy cream, the Parmesan cheese, and the garlic powder until smooth.
Squeeze the spinach dry and add it. Blend again. Add the drained artichoke hearts and pulse until they are coarsely chopped.
Scrape the mixture into a heavy covered pot. Cook on low heat for 75 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the center is hot.
Scatter the Monterey Jack cheese over the top and spoon the salsa around the edge. Cover and cook 15 minutes more until the Monterey Jack cheese melts.
Warm the flour tortillas so they bend. Brush a skillet with the vegetable oil and set it over medium-low heat.
Lay a flour tortilla in the skillet, add a handful of the meltable cheese and a scoop of the hot spinach mixture, and cover with a second flour tortilla.

Cook until the underside has a few brown spots and the meltable cheese melts, about 3 minutes. Flip and cook 2 minutes more until the quesadilla holds together. Repeat with the remaining flour tortillas. Cut into wedges.

attribution.note: Dip cooked, then folded into the quesadilla. Dip scaled to about a quarter so it fills 4 quesadillas. A covered pot stands in for the slow cooker, for the same time. Vegetable oil used where the quesadilla page allows oil or cooking spray. Optional quesadilla fillings other than this dip were left out. Crackers were left out because the dip goes into the tortillas.

name: Baked Brie in Puff Pastry
steps: Let the Brie cheese sit at room temperature and trim off the rind. Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Season the Brie cheese on all sides with the salt and the black pepper.
Lay the puff pastry flat. Set the Brie cheese in the center.
Trim about 1/2 inch from the edges of the puff pastry if the sheet is much larger than the cheese. Fold the puff pastry over the Brie cheese.
Beat the egg. Brush the last fold with egg so the pastry seals, then brush the top with the remaining egg.
Bake for 15 minutes until the puff pastry is deep golden. Cool 10 minutes before cutting.

attribution.note: Odd roasted-grape snack replaced with baked brie. Salt and black pepper are in the ingredient list even though the method lines skip them, so they season the Brie cheese. Yield kept at 4 snack servings from one wheel.

name: Kimchi Fried Rice
steps: Break the cooked rice apart so the grains are separate. Chop the kimchi and slice the scallions.
Warm 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the eggs for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft. Move them to a plate.
Add the remaining vegetable oil. Cook the kimchi for 2 minutes until it smells sharp and the edges soften.
Add the cooked rice, the kimchi juice, and the soy sauce. Toss over medium-high heat for 4 minutes until the grains are hot and a few edges crisp.
Stir in the sesame oil and the scallions.
Top each bowl with a fried egg.

attribution.note: No kimchi fried rice page. Cabbage Kimchi is the pickle, not the rice dish.
